transcript.content: Hello. I am Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I keep making myself throw up after I eat. I've been doing it a lot. Sometimes I'll go into the bathroom at work, or I'll do it right when I get home. I really hate it, but... it's just started feeling like it's the only way I can actually calm down.
When you eat before throwing up, do you feel like you are eating an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?

Yeah, I do. It's definitely a lot. When it happens, I can go through a full bag of chips, some pastries from the corner store, whatever leftovers are in the fridge, and a bunch of sweet drinks... all in just one sitting. It's like I don't even really notice how much food is actually gone until I finally stop.
When you engage in this behavior of throwing up, does it always happen after you have eaten that large amount of food, or do you sometimes do it after eating only a small or normal-sized meal?

I... I'm not really sure, honestly. I know for a fact I do it after eating all that food at once, like I was saying. But as for just a regular-sized meal or a small snack... I haven't really paid attention to whether I do it then, too. I just haven't noticed.
During those times when you eat a large amount of food, do you feel like you are unable to stop eating or unable to control how much you are eating?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Once I start, it's like... I just can't stop. It feels like my hands just keep reaching for more food, even while I'm in my head telling myself to quit. It's almost like I'm just watching myself do it, and I can't make myself stop no matter how hard I try.
Besides throwing up, do you use any other methods to try to prevent weight gain, such as taking laxatives, fasting for long periods, or exercising excessively?

Yeah, I do some other things. On the days after I end up eating too much like that, I try to make up for it. I'll usually try not to eat anything at all until really late in the day. And I try to exercise, too. I'll go for long walks or just push myself to work out, even when my legs are already aching from standing all day at the dry cleaners. I just feel like I have to do something to balance it out.
How do you feel about your body shape or your weight when you look in the mirror?

Honestly, it pretty much controls how I feel about myself. Like, I can be doing really good at the shop, getting all the clothes done and having a fine day... but if I just happen to catch my reflection in the front glass and my stomach or my hips look big to me, it ruins everything. I instantly feel like a complete failure. It's hard to look in the mirror because I just really don't like my shape or my weight at all.
On average, how many times per week would you say you engage in this cycle of eating a large amount of food and then trying to get rid of it?

Well, for months now, I'd say most weeks have at least a couple of episodes... usually more, to be honest. It's just this constant cycle where I eat way more than I ever meant to, and then I have to try and undo it by throwing up, or fasting, or exercising it off. But yeah, it happens at least a couple of times a week, every week.
